programme: A barrier-permeability/NF-κB-restraint module: HDAC1 epigenetically silences inflammatory and junctional target genes, NKRF acts as the direct transcriptional brake on NF-κB (targets include CXCL8, PTGS2/COX2, GCLC/GCLM), and MECOM sits upstream of tight-junction and angiopoietin-Tie2 vascular-permeability genes (CLDN1, ANGPT1/ANGPT2, TEK, SERPINE1). SNAI1's target set (CDH1, CLDN1, CLDN3, VIM) is the classic EMT/junction-remodeling executor of the same genes MECOM and NKRF converge on, though no retrieved paper places SNAI1 in either disease.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's, HDAC1 is reported to mediate blood-brain-barrier permeability (38329647), and gut-derived short-chain fatty acids act through HDAC to reduce Tau hyperphosphorylation (40812734) — a direct epigenetic gut-to-brain link. NKRF's NF-κB-repressing activity is reported dysregulated in AD (38738952), and MECOM is proposed as a blood biomarker tied to energy metabolism in AD (39093073).
role_in_b: In IBS, HDAC1 is implicated by network-pharmacology and epigenetic-enzyme studies of intestinal cells (42500261, 41355505). NKRF is a direct target of miR-29 alongside Claudin-1, and its loss increases intestinal permeability (25277410); NKRF-adjacent NLRP3 inflammasome activity drives inflammation in an IBS-D model that paeoniflorin reverses (36590561). MECOM has no IBS-specific record, but its target CLDN1 is the same tight-junction gene implicated by the NKRF/miR-29 paper.
shared_axis: Both a colorectal epithelium and a cerebral vascular endothelium depend on the same tight-junction/NF-κB-restraint circuitry to stay sealed; if HDAC1, NKRF and MECOM run this circuit in both tissues, a systemic perturbation (chronic low-grade inflammation, or a microbiome-derived signal such as SCFAs acting through HDAC1) could loosen gut junctions and the BBB in parallel, giving a mechanistic reason IBS-associated barrier and inflammatory changes could co-occur with AD-associated BBB breakdown and neuroinflammation.
reasoning: HDAC1 and NKRF are each independently placed by name in both diseases, and NKRF's disease-B paper and MECOM's target list converge on the same gene (CLDN1), which is unusually convergent for this dataset — only 4 of 12 concordant factors have any literature at all, and 3 of those 4 are the ones carrying this programme. No retrieved paper studies AD and IBS together through this axis, so the pairing itself is inferred rather than stated, which caps the verdict at 'supported' rather than 'established'.
support: 38329647 — HDAC1 mediates blood-brain-barrier permeability in an in vitro AD model; 40812734 — SCFA supplementation reduces Tau hyperphosphorylation via HDAC-linked mechanism in AD; 42500261 — network-pharmacology study places HDAC1 in an IBS treatment mechanism; 41355505 — epigenetic regulatory enzymes including HDAC1 studied in intestinal cells relevant to IBS; 38738952 — NKRF (with ZBTB17) regulates NF-κB signaling in AD; 36590561 — paeoniflorin lowers NLRP3-driven inflammation in an IBS-D model (NKRF-adjacent NF-κB axis); 25277410 — miR-29 targets NKRF and Claudin-1 together to increase intestinal permeability in IBS; 39093073 — MECOM proposed as an AD blood biomarker tied to energy metabolism. SNAI1: none found placing it in either disease.
how_to_falsify: In a microbiome-humanized mouse model carrying both AD pathology (e.g., APP/PS1) and an IBS-like visceral-hypersensitivity phenotype, knock down HDAC1 and NKRF intestine-specifically and measure whether Claudin-1/tight-junction integrity and NF-κB target expression change in the gut but blood-brain-barrier permeability and Tau phosphorylation remain unchanged (or vice versa with a brain-specific knockdown) — if the two compartments respond independently rather than concordantly, the shared-programme claim fails.
caveats: Only 3 independent cohort pairs underlie the 32 patient-group comparisons, so replication is thinner than the comparison count suggests. HDAC1, NKRF and MECOM support (21/32, 20/32, 21/32) are not the top-recurring factors in the list (TFAP4 at 24/32 has none of the same evidentiary support), so the choice of carrying factors rests on literature coherence, not recurrence rank. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed ZEB1 (SNAI1's usual EMT partner) and HDAC7 (an HDAC1 paralog) as ordinary for brain/gut tissue pairs generally — meaning the general EMT/HDAC signature is not distinctive to this pair, and only the specific presence of SNAI1/HDAC1 (rather than ZEB1/HDAC7) argues this recurred non-generically here. No retrieved paper ties any of these factors to both diseases within a single study.
